name: BPMO + Proof Points
description: The default Xcamp backcasting framework. Structures any project as a tree of objectives under four invariant dimensions (Business, Product, Market, Operations) and 22 canonical categories, with 7 archetype overlays for common project types. Each category carries a typed, stage-tagged proof-points catalog so generated objectives arrive pre-seeded with their expected evidence tasks. The proof model credits six evidence types — strategy, validation, capability, relationship, artifact, traction — so early-stage projects are scored on stage-appropriate signal rather than KPIs they could not yet have. Ontology anchored to: Business Model Canvas, APQC PCF, Porter, STP/4Ps/7Ps, TAM/SAM/SOM, SCOR, OKRs, IRIS+, AARRR.

levels.label: Dimension
levels.description: Invariant top-level axis. Written to objectives.dimension.

levels.label: Category
levels.description: The unit that maps to one Xcamp objective. Written to objectives.category. Carries the proof-points catalog.

structure.depth_note: Two-level hierarchy (dimension → category). The proof_density parameter controls how many objectives are generated per category, not the structural depth of the framework itself.

types.demonstrates: A reasoned, documented decision or bet — judgment before results
External/market evidence that reduces a risk
Demonstrated internal skill, process, or de-risked hard problem
A tangible document/asset that demonstrably exists
Quantitative results — the classic investor KPI

proof_model.ladder_note: Each proof point carries the earliest stage it typically appears. The generation step focuses proof tasks at stage <= current_stage + 1 so a pre-seed project sees idea + pre_seed catalog entries and seed entries only when they are blocking the next milestone. early_signal=true marks counter-intuitive progress that investors rarely see clearly at that stage.

generation.interpretation_prompt:
You are an expert at interpreting startup and project briefs for structured decomposition using the BPMO framework (Business · Product · Market · Operations).

Your task: read the project brief and extract a structured interpretation that the decomposition engine will use in the next step. Output ONLY valid JSON — no preamble, no markdown fences, nothing else.

## Archetype definitions
{{ARCHETYPE_DEFINITIONS_JSON}}

## Stage definitions
- idea       : pre-formation; thesis exists, no team or product yet
- pre_seed   : team forming, problem validated, prototype or early concept
- seed       : MVP built or in market, early customers, raising first institutional round
- growth     : product-market fit found, scaling revenue or users

## Output schema (output exactly this shape)
{
  "project_name": "inferred or stated project name",
  "archetype_slug": "one of the archetype slugs above",
  "archetype_confidence": 0.0 to 1.0,
  "archetype_rationale": "one sentence explaining the archetype choice",
  "stage": "idea | pre_seed | seed | growth",
  "stage_confidence": 0.0 to 1.0,
  "stage_rationale": "one sentence explaining the stage choice",
  "value_proposition": "concise statement of the core value offered",
  "target_customer": "who the primary customer or beneficiary is",
  "key_risks": ["up to five biggest risks as short noun phrases"],
  "dimension_emphasis": {
    "note": "any dimensions that should receive extra or reduced focus given this project type",
    "overweight": ["dimension slugs"],
    "underweight": ["dimension slugs"]
  },
  "constraints": "any explicit constraints, deadlines, or context from the brief worth preserving"
}

## Project brief
{{RAW_INPUT}}
generation.generation_prompt:
You are an expert project decomposition assistant working within the BPMO + Proof Points backcasting framework (Business · Product · Market · Operations, version {{FRAMEWORK_VERSION}}).

## Your task
Decompose the project brief into a structured tree of objectives, one per relevant category, each pre-seeded with the expected proof tasks from the framework catalog. The output will be reviewed and edited by the founder before being committed to the platform — treat it as a rigorous first draft, not a finished plan.

## Project context (from interpretation step)
{{INTERPRETATION_JSON}}

## Project stage
{{PROJECT_STAGE}}

## Resolved category set for this archetype
The following categories are active for this project. Each carries a proof_points catalog — the framework's expected evidence for that category.
{{RESOLVED_CATEGORIES_JSON}}

## Rules for objectives
1. Produce one objective per category that is materially relevant to this project at its current stage. You may omit a category only if it is genuinely not applicable (e.g. a pure-software project has no manufacturing objective). Never omit a category just because it is hard or early.
2. Title: outcome-oriented, specific to this project (not the generic category label). Max 12 words.
3. Description: 2–3 sentences explaining what achieving this objective means for this specific project, the current context, and why it matters at this stage.
4. dimension and category: copy the exact slugs from the resolved category set. These are immutable framework identifiers.

## Rules for proof_tasks
Proof tasks are the evidence the founder must deliver to demonstrate progress on the objective. They come in two kinds:

### source: "framework" tasks (required)
- For every proof_point in the category's catalog whose stage is at or before the NEXT stage beyond the current project stage, produce one proof task.
  - Example: project is at pre_seed → include idea + pre_seed proof points; include seed proof points only if they are already partially begun or are blocking the next funding step.
- Title: contextualise the generic catalog label to this specific project (use project names, numbers, actual customers, domain specifics). Keep under 15 words.
- CRITICAL: copy proof_type, stage, and early_signal VERBATIM from the catalog entry. Do not invent or alter these fields for source:"framework" tasks.

### source: "ai" tasks (optional additions)
- You may add project-specific proof tasks not in the catalog, for anything important to this project that the generic catalog does not cover.
- Choose proof_type and stage that honestly reflect what the task demonstrates and when it is achievable.
- Use sparingly — the catalog already covers the framework's expectations. Add only what is genuinely novel.

## Rules for notes (optional)
You may add up to two notes per objective for context, rationale, or links to key risks. note_type must be one of: "note", "insight", "context".

## Retrieved context
{{RETRIEVED_CONTEXT}}

---

## Output format
Output ONLY valid JSON matching the output schema exactly — no preamble, no markdown fences, nothing else.
{{OUTPUT_SCHEMA_JSON}}

interpretation.ARCHETYPE_DEFINITIONS_JSON: engine_inject: array of {slug, label, example} from taxonomy.archetypes

generation.RESOLVED_CATEGORIES_JSON: engine_inject: effective category set after applying archetype overlay (base_categories minus remove_categories, plus add_categories, with override_categories applied). Each entry includes slug, label, scope, and the full proof_points array. Emphasis weights are NOT injected into the prompt — they are used by the qualify calc, not the generator.
generation.RETRIEVED_CONTEXT: vox_inject: open and licensed reference content retrieved by Vox /backcaster/generate from Rewind (reference_content + licensed_content source_types), domain-scoped to the resolved category set. Access-filtered per user. Empty string if Rewind is in stub mode.

determinism_guardrail.description: After generation, the engine enforces this contract on every source:'framework' proof task: if the returned proof_type or stage does not exactly match the catalog entry for that proof_point label and category, the engine overwrites it from the catalog. This keeps the proof taxonomy trustworthy regardless of model drift. The engine identifies the catalog entry by (category, proof_point index) — framework tasks are emitted in catalog order before any source:'ai' tasks.

content_model.description: All AI generation routes through Vox (chiapi.xchange.eco), not direct OpenAI. Vox performs two retrieval passes before calling OpenAI: (1) user workspace context from Rewind (source_types: project, objective, note, backcaster_version); (2) reference content from semantic_documents (entity_type: reference_content or licensed_content), domain-scoped to the resolved category set via semantic_tags.

reference_content_source.domain_scoping: semantic_tags[] carries category slugs; Vox biases retrieval by these
reference_content_source.first_seed: 22 BPMO category descriptions seeded from ontology by seed-frameworks.ts
reference_content_source.vox_source_type: reference_content and licensed_content rows in memory_sources (Vox local DB migration 009)

archetype_detection.description: The interpretation step infers archetype_slug and archetype_confidence from the brief. The engine then surfaces a HITL confirm card: 'I read this as a [archetype label] — does that look right?' with alternatives. The confirmed archetype resolves the effective category set before generation. This follows the existing AIProposal propose→confirm pattern.

stage_detection.description: Stage is inferred from the brief (via the interpretation step) and confirmed by the founder via a single-question HITL step before generation. Inferred stage is preferred over founder declaration because it is harder to game: a project with no proof tasks delivered in idea-stage categories should not self-declare as seed.

proof_metadata_shape._pq_note: pq_cache and pq_at are null at seed time; populated by the Qualify service on first read and cached until notes.updated_at advances.

rpc_map.objective: create_objective(project_id, title, description, dimension, category, detail)

qualify_integration.description: The Qualify funnel reads objectives.dimension (wave-graph lane), objectives.category (comparison axis), and per-task proof signals. notes.done=true is the binary delivery gate. Additional note attributes — content length, linked notes, attachments — weight the quality of each delivered proof, producing a per-category coverage_score * quality_score composite. Low-evidence or low-quality categories render as wide translucent bands on the wave graph; high-certainty delivered categories as tight ridgelines. Comparison requires matching framework_slug + framework_version.

proof_quality_model._description: proof_quality is a 0.0–1.0 score computed at Qualify read time from live note attributes. It is NOT stored permanently — it is cached in notes.detail under 'pq_cache' with a 'pq_at' timestamp and invalidated whenever the note is updated (trigger or app-layer). notes.done=true is always the binary gate: a task that is not done has proof_quality=0 regardless of content. A task that IS done has proof_quality in [0.1, 1.0] depending on quality signals.

delivery_gate.rule: done=false → proof_quality=0.0, task is not counted as delivered
delivery_gate.rule_done: done=true  → compute proof_quality from signals below, minimum 0.1

content.rationale: Substance of the proof write-up. A blank or one-line mark-done scores near zero; a full explanation of what was learned, built, or agreed scores higher. Threshold is generous — we want to reward writing, not punish brevity.

sources: note_links WHERE link_type IN ('attachment','proof','ref') FROM this note
count of <a href> tags in notes.body_html as url_count
artifact.formula: raw = attachment_count * ATTACHMENT_WEIGHT + url_count * URL_WEIGHT; artifact_score = min(1.0, raw)
artifact.rationale: Tangible assets — a deck, a spreadsheet, a signed document, a prototype link — carry more evidential weight than prose. An attachment (preferred_external_container_id or a linked note with link_type='attachment') scores more than a bare URL in body text.

sources: COUNT(note_links WHERE from_note_id = task.id OR to_note_id = task.id)
COUNT(objective_notes WHERE note_id = task.id) — note linked to >1 objective
links.rationale: Cross-referencing shows the proof integrates with the broader project — a task linked to other notes (related decisions, supporting evidence) or referenced by multiple objectives shows higher epistemic value than an isolated completed task. One link raises it noticeably; three saturates.

early_signal_multiplier.rationale: An early-signal proof point — the kind of counter-intuitive, strategy-or-learning evidence that investors rarely see — carries extra weight in the funnel when actually delivered with substance. The multiplier is modest (15%) and capped at 1.0 so it rewards early thoroughness without distorting the overall score.

proof_quality_model.final_formula: proof_quality = min(1.0, base * (1.15 if early_signal and base > 0 else 1.0)); if done=false: proof_quality = 0.0; if done=true and base=0: proof_quality = 0.1  (floor for minimal completion credit)

cache.invalidation: cleared whenever notes row is updated (updated_at trigger or app layer)
cache.read_policy: use cached value if pq_at >= notes.updated_at, else recompute and cache

proof_quality_model.additional_index: notes_proof_done_idx ON notes (done) WHERE note_type='task' AND detail->>'kind'='proof'

category_scoring._description: Coverage and quality are separate terms. Separating them keeps the wave graph honest: a category with three done tasks but all minimal completions shows high coverage and low quality (a warning), while one done task with a rich artifact shows low coverage but high quality (a promising signal).

per_category.eligible_tasks: All tasks WHERE detail->>'kind'='proof' AND detail->>'category'=slug AND detail->>'stage' <= stage_ordering[project_stage + 1]

coverage_score.formula: count(done=true eligible tasks) / count(all eligible tasks)
coverage_score.meaning: What fraction of expected proof has been delivered at all

quality_score.formula: mean(proof_quality for done=true eligible tasks)  [0.0 if none done]
quality_score.meaning: How thoroughly the delivered proof is evidenced

category_score.meaning: Combined signal: did they deliver AND is it substantiated

certainty.formula: evidence_density = count(done=true eligible tasks) / max(1, count(all eligible tasks)); mapping_confidence = from semantic alignment step (min 0 if no objective, max 1 if exact slug match); certainty = 0.6 * evidence_density + 0.4 * mapping_confidence
certainty.meaning: How confident the funnel is in the category_score. Low certainty = wide translucent band on the wave graph. High certainty = tight ridgeline.

headline.overall_certainty: mean(certainty) across all categories with >= 1 eligible task

proof_read_query.filter: note_type = 'task' AND detail->>'kind' = 'proof' AND detail->>'framework_slug' = 'bpmo-proof' AND done = true  -- gate applied at query level for coverage calc;                     fetch all (done + not-done) for coverage denominator
join_for_quality: LEFT JOIN note_links nl ON nl.from_note_id = notes.id OR nl.to_note_id = notes.id
LEFT JOIN objective_notes on2 ON on2.note_id = notes.id  -- count cross-objective refs
indexes_required: notes_proof_done_idx     ON notes (done)                     WHERE note_type='task' AND detail->>'kind'='proof'

versioning.description: A published framework version is never mutated. A new semver row is inserted. Qualification runs record the version they used; comparability requires the same version or an explicit migration map. Patch (x.y.Z): proof-point label corrections, scope clarifications, no slug changes. Minor (x.Y.0): new categories or archetypes added; existing slugs unchanged. Major (X.0.0): dimension or category slug changes; migration map required.
